name: Operation Dark Winter (JHU/CSIS)
description: June 2001 senior-level tabletop exercise simulating a covert smallpox bioterrorist attack on the United States. Conducted by Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security and the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS). Revealed critical systemic weaknesses in US public health preparedness and response capacity.
reputation: historically significant; frequently cited in US biodefense and public health preparedness literature
notes: Open access materials. Preceded 9/11 and anthrax attacks; findings shaped US biodefense policy. Part of JHU CHS historical exercise series.

institutions: Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security
Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS)
